source.publication: NOAA Climate Prediction Center — ENSO advisory

description: The ENSO regime flipped: NOAA upgraded to an El Nino Advisory on 2026-06-11 with a ~63% chance of a VERY STRONG ('super') El Nino in the Nov-Jan window (ECMWF Nino3.4 possibly >2.5C by October) — potentially the 4th super El Nino in 30 years. This inverts the prior La-Nina base case that most 2025 soft-commodity studies assumed. A super El Nino pressures tropical softs UP — cocoa, food oils, rice, sugar, robusta coffee — with tail-risk estimates of +50-100% on the most-exposed crops (cocoa spiked to ~$4,700/t in May before easing to ~$3,850/t). The impact is crop-split: El Nino typically HELPS US/Argentina/Brazil soybean yields (+2-5%) while hurting tropical softs and Asian rice, so a broad softs basket (DBA) benefits unevenly. Directly relevant to agriculture_soft_commodities: a supply-shock catalyst that raises soft prices, with the peak physical impact lagging 6-12 months into 2027. Treated as a BUILDING event (long half-life) that strengthens as the winter event confirms. NOTE: this inverts the stored agriculture_soft_commodities study thesis (assumed 71% La Nina) — flag that study for /catalyx-sector-study refresh.
